nodes.name: RhPd-H one-pot solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The RhPd-H was synthesized through a one-pot solvothermal method by the simultaneous reduction of Rh(acac)₃ and Pd(acac)₂ in formaldehyde solution. Formaldehyde can be decomposed into hydrogen gas on metal catalysts (HCHO → H₂ + CO), and then the in situ generated hydrogen molecules can be dissociated into H atoms on Pd surfaces with a little or no activation energy barrier.
nodes.source_text: The RhPd-H was synthesized through a one-pot solvothermal method by the simultaneous reduction of Rh(acac)₃ and Pd(acac)₂ in formaldehyde solution... Pd has a modest binding of H, and Rh does not bind H, while the RhPd system strongly binds H.

nodes.procedure: The RhPd-H was annealed at 300°C in Ar condition for 3 h to investigate the effect from the confined H atoms. The obtained catalyst (RhPd-H/C-A) is RhPd alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: RhPd-H exhibits dominant sheet-like morphology with roughly flat surface, some wrinkles, and ultrathin nature indicated by low contrast.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the RhPd-H was characterized by high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM, Figure 2a) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Figure S1). The products have dominant sheet-like morphology that presents a roughly flat surface, with some wrinkles. The RhPd-H particles exhibit a quite low contrast against the background, indicating that they are ultrathin.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms ultrathin character of RhPd-H nanosheets with thickness higher than TEM measurement due to residual capping agent.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ultrathin character was further confirmed by atomic force microscopy (AFM) images and corresponding height profiles (Figure 2c).

properties.bars: Red histogram bars showing thickness distribution

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows Rh and Pd are distributed uniformly through the RhPd-H sheets indicating metallic alloy structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping show that the Rh and Pd are distributed uniformly through the sheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS detects hydrogenation state of RhPd-H with measured peak at 4.46 eV matching reported metal-hydride systems; small shake up at 6 eV in valence spectra from XPS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) was further performed to detect the hydrogenation state of the RhPd-H (Figures 2g and S3). The measured EELS peak was 4.46 eV, which matches well with results in reported metal-hydride systems. The interaction between the Rh/Pd 4d and H 1s states results in a small shake up appeared at 6 eV in the valence spectra of the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurement.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution HAADF-STEM shows average lattice spacing of RhPd-H is 0.230 nm, 3.6% larger than Rh6Pd4 alloy (0.222 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-resolution HAADF-STEM images indicate that the average lattice spacing of the RhPd-H is 0.230 nm (Figure 2h,i), which is about 3.6% larger than that expected for the normal Rh6Pd4 alloy nanostructures (0.222 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of RhPd-H show no obvious changes after 6 months ambient storage; peaks shift to lower angles indicating expanded crystal lattices due to interstitial H atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: There were no obvious changes on XRD patterns of the RhPdH after 6 months (Figure 4a,b) ... the measured XRD peaks shifted to lower angles during the reaction, indicating the expanded crystal lattices (Figure 3h).
